data.title: Complete Umrah Guide
data.description: Umrah can be performed at any time of the year and takes a few hours. The Prophet ﷺ said: "From one Umrah to the next is an expiation for what is between them, and an accepted Hajj has no reward but Paradise" (Sahih al-Bukhari 1773, Sahih Muslim 1349), and "Umrah in Ramadan is equal to Hajj" (Sahih al-Bukhari 1782, Sahih Muslim 1256). It has four parts: ihram, tawaf, sa'i, and shaving or trimming the hair.

sections.title: 1. Enter Ihram at the Miqat
sections.content:
Bathe, men put on the two white sheets, women wear their ordinary modest clothing, and before passing the miqat make the intention:

لَبَّيْكَ عُمْرَةً

"Here I am, for Umrah." Then repeat the Talbiyah until you begin tawaf.

If you fear something will stop you completing it (illness, for example), you may add: "If anything prevents me, my place of release is wherever You stop me" (Sahih al-Bukhari 5089, Sahih Muslim 1207).

The miqats and the rules of ihram are explained in Ihram & Miqat.

Prepared from the Qur'an and authentic Sunnah, following the position of the majority of scholars. Where your madhhab, your scholar or your Hajj operator directs otherwise, follow them.

sections.title: 2. Tawaf: Seven Circuits of the Ka'bah
sections.content:
Enter al-Masjid al-Haram with the right foot and the du'a for entering the masjid. Be in wudu for tawaf.

  1. Men uncover the right shoulder (idtiba'), passing the upper sheet under the right arm.
  2. Start at the Black Stone: touch or kiss it if you can without harming anyone; otherwise face it and raise your right hand, saying Allahu akbar (Sahih al-Bukhari 1613).
  3. Walk seven circuits with the Ka'bah on your left. Men walk briskly (raml) in the first three circuits if they can (Sahih Muslim 1262).
  4. There is no fixed dhikr for each circuit: recite Qur'an, remember Allah, and ask for what you need in any language.
  5. Between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone, say: "Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire" (Qur'an 2:201; Sunan Abi Dawud 1892).
  6. After the seventh circuit, cover the shoulder again and pray two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim if there is room, or anywhere in the masjid, reciting Surah al-Kafirun and Surah al-Ikhlas (Sahih Muslim 1218; Qur'an 2:125).
  7. Drink Zamzam.

Prepared from the Qur'an and authentic Sunnah, following the position of the majority of scholars. Where your madhhab, your scholar or your Hajj operator directs otherwise, follow them.

sections.title: 3. Sa'i between Safa and Marwah
sections.content:
Go to Safa. On approaching it, recite: "Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah" (Qur'an 2:158), and say: "I begin with what Allah began with" (Sahih Muslim 1218).

  1. Climb Safa, face the Ka'bah, raise your hands, and say the dhikr of Safa three times, making du'a in between (see At Safa and Marwah).
  2. Walk to Marwah. Men run between the two green lights; women walk.
  3. At Marwah, do as you did at Safa. That is one lap.
  4. Seven laps in all: Safa to Marwah is one, Marwah back to Safa is two. You finish at Marwah.

Wudu is recommended for sa'i but not required, so a woman who begins her period after tawaf may complete her sa'i.

Prepared from the Qur'an and authentic Sunnah, following the position of the majority of scholars. Where your madhhab, your scholar or your Hajj operator directs otherwise, follow them.

sections.title: 4. Shave or Trim the Hair
sections.content:
Men shave the head or trim the hair from all over it; shaving is better (Sahih al-Bukhari 1727). Women gather their hair and cut a fingertip's length from the end.

With this your Umrah is complete, and everything forbidden by ihram is lawful again. If you are on Hajj Tamattu' and Hajj is close, many scholars recommend trimming now and leaving the shaving for the 10th of Dhul Hijjah.

May Allah accept your Umrah.

Prepared from the Qur'an and authentic Sunnah, following the position of the majority of scholars. Where your madhhab, your scholar or your Hajj operator directs otherwise, follow them.

checklists.title: Documents
items: Passport valid for at least 6 months from your travel date
Hajj or Umrah visa, issued through a licensed operator (Hajj permits are issued through Nusuk)
Meningococcal (ACWY) vaccination certificate, and any other vaccines the Saudi Ministry of Health requires for your year
Printed and phone copies of passport, visa, tickets and hotel booking
Your operator's contact numbers, and your group leader's name
Your national ID and a few passport photos

checklists.title: Packing
items: Men: two sets of ihram (two white unsewn sheets each) and a belt or pouch
Women: loose, modest everyday clothing; no niqab or gloves while in ihram
Unscented soap, shampoo, deodorant and lotion for the days of ihram
Comfortable sandals that leave the top of the foot uncovered, and a spare pair
Small bag or bottle for the pebbles
Light prayer mat, small Qur'an, and a list of your duas
Umbrella for shade, refillable water bottle, power bank

checklists.title: Health
items: Your regular medicines, enough for the whole trip, with prescriptions
Oral rehydration salts, plasters and blister pads, pain relief
Unscented sunscreen and lip balm
Face masks for the crowds
A letter from your doctor if you have a chronic condition

checklists.title: Money & Debts
items: Pay for Hajj from wealth you know to be halal
Settle debts, or arrange them with your creditors, before you go
Leave enough for your family's needs while you are away
Carry some cash in Saudi riyals and a card that works abroad
Budget for the sacrifice (hady) if your Hajj is Tamattu' or Qiran

checklists.title: Spiritual Preparation
items: Make your intention purely for Allah
Repent, and ask forgiveness from anyone you have wronged
Write your will (wasiyyah)
Learn the rites before you travel; this guide is a start
Write down the people who asked you for du'a
Resolve to avoid argument, obscenity and sin (Qur'an 2:197)
